RustXMALab for Linux (x86_64)
=============================

This archive holds two programs and a menu entry for them:

  rustxmalab          the window program (a rewrite of XMALab 3)
  xma                 the command-line program (information, recompute,
                      export, edit, calibrate, track, parity)
  rustxmalab.desktop  the menu entry for the window program
  rustxmalab.png      the menu entry's picture

Installing
----------

Unpack the archive anywhere and run the programs from that folder, or copy
them to a folder on your PATH (for example ~/.local/bin). Nothing else is
installed and nothing needs to be built.

  ./rustxmalab                  start the window program
  ./rustxmalab project.xma      open a project
  ./xma info project.xma        what a project contains
  ./xma --help                  the commands of the command-line program

To add RustXMALab to the desktop's application menu by hand:
copy rustxmalab.desktop to ~/.local/share/applications/ and rustxmalab.png to
~/.local/share/icons/hicolor/256x256/apps/, and make sure rustxmalab is on
your PATH (or put its full path in the desktop file's Exec= line).

Settings are kept in ~/.config/RustXMALab/settings.json (or under
$XDG_CONFIG_HOME). XMALab's own settings are never read or changed.

What the programs need on the machine
-------------------------------------

Both programs link only to the C library (glibc: libc, libm, libgcc_s). They
need the glibc version of the machine they were built on, or newer:

  rustxmalab   glibc @GLIBC_rustxmalab@ or newer
  xma          glibc @GLIBC_xma@ or newer

(Check yours with `ldd --version`.)

xma needs nothing more.

rustxmalab loads these system libraries when it opens its window. They are part
of every Linux desktop; on a server or a minimal install, install them with
your package manager:

  Window system, Wayland:  libwayland-client.so.0, libxkbcommon.so.0
  Window system, X11:      libX11.so.6, libX11-xcb.so.1, libxcb.so.1,
                           libXcursor.so.1, libXi.so.6, libxkbcommon.so.0,
                           libxkbcommon-x11.so.0
  Graphics:                libvulkan.so.1 with a Vulkan driver for the
                           graphics card (Mesa, or the vendor's driver), or
                           else libEGL.so.1 with an OpenGL ES 3 driver

The program uses Wayland when it runs in a Wayland session and X11
otherwise; only the libraries for the one in use are needed.

Debian or Ubuntu:  sudo apt install libwayland-client0 libxkbcommon0
                   libxkbcommon-x11-0 libx11-6 libx11-xcb1 libxcursor1 libxi6
                   libvulkan1 mesa-vulkan-drivers
Fedora:            sudo dnf install libwayland-client libxkbcommon
                   libxkbcommon-x11 libX11 libX11-xcb libXcursor libXi
                   vulkan-loader mesa-vulkan-drivers

Video files
-----------

Uncompressed and MJPEG AVI files, Phantom .cine files and image sequences
(TIFF, PNG, JPEG, BMP) are read by the programs themselves.

Other video formats (for example H.264 or HEVC in .mp4, .mov or .avi) are
read through FFmpeg: the programs run the ffmpeg and ffprobe executables
installed on the machine. Install FFmpeg with your package manager
(sudo apt install ffmpeg, or sudo dnf install ffmpeg), or put ffmpeg and
ffprobe next to the programs, or name them with the environment variables
XMALAB_FFMPEG and XMALAB_FFPROBE. FFmpeg is not part of this archive and is
not needed for the formats listed above.
